original_question: Characterize the unlabelled graphs H for which, for every n, the largest H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] has size exactly 2^{C(n,2)-e(H)}, equivalently, for which every maximum H-intersecting family can be obtained by fixing one copy of H and taking all graphs that contain it. In particular, determine whether every critical graph H has this Erdős-Ko-Rado property.
target_in_paper: Section 4, final unlabeled open problem immediately after Conjecture 4.6: characterize the unlabelled graphs H with the Erdős-Ko-Rado property for H, and in particular test the conjectural sufficient condition that H be critical. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main target: the paper’s end-of-section characterization problem for unlabelled graphs H with g_H(n) = 2^{binom(n,2)-e(H)} for every n, together with the follow-up conjectural direction that critical graphs should suffice. It also correctly identifies the standard 'fix one copy of H' extremal construction. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
missing_details: The paper first defines g_H(n) by g_H(n) := max{|F| : F is an H-intersecting family of graphs on [n]}; that notation should be included to make the question stand alone. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

It should explicitly say that H is a fixed unlabelled graph, while the families F consist of labelled graphs on the vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n}. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

It should define 'H-intersecting': for every G1,G2 in F, the graph G1 ∩ G2 contains a copy of H. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The paper’s equivalence is existential, not universal: it says that for each n, a maximum-sized H-intersecting family can be obtained by fixing a copy of H and taking all graphs containing it. Your draft strengthens this to 'every maximum H-intersecting family', which is not what the paper states. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The critical-graph clause should include the paper’s definition: H is critical if every proper subgraph of H has smaller chromatic number than H. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The quantifier is 'for every n in N'; there is no asymptotic weakening such as 'for all sufficiently large n'. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be framed as the Erdős-Ko-Rado property for H, exactly as the paper names it. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

No extra algebraic structure, field, ring, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions are involved here; the setting is purely graph-theoretic. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
refined_question: For a fixed unlabelled graph H, let g_H(n) := max{|F| : F is an H-intersecting family of labelled graphs on [n]}, where F is H-intersecting if G1 ∩ G2 contains a copy of H for every G1,G2 in F. Characterize those unlabelled graphs H for which, for every n in N, one has g_H(n) = 2^{binom(n,2)-e(H)}; equivalently, for every n there exists a maximum-sized H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] consisting of all graphs that contain some fixed copy of H. In the paper’s terminology, for which H does H have the Erdős-Ko-Rado property, and is every critical graph H (meaning every proper subgraph of H has smaller chromatic number than H) guaranteed to have this property? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
equivalent_formulation: Characterize the unlabelled graphs H such that, for every n in N, there exists a maximum-sized H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] obtained by fixing a copy of H and taking all graphs on [n] that contain that copy. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the last paragraph of Section 4, not Conjecture 4.1 itself: that paragraph explicitly asks to characterize the unlabelled graphs H with g_H(n) = 2^{binom(n,2)-e(H)} for all n, introduces the name 'Erdős-Ko-Rado property for H', and immediately adds the conjectural sufficient condition that H be critical. Conjecture 4.1 and Proposition 4.2 are relevant nearby context because they define the clique case and the surrounding notation/strengthening framework, but the exact target is the final unlabeled characterization problem after Conjecture 4.6. The only substantive mismatch in the draft is that it replaces the paper’s existential extremal-family formulation ('a maximum-sized family can be obtained this way') with a stronger uniqueness-type claim about every maximum family. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
